messages.subject: Re: Changes in sampling intervals
parts:
Hi Adam,

Your dt=15 %#% 'min' case is different from the dt=2 %#% 'hour' case, because the latter is a bad approximation of the true sampling schedule and so a bad objective function is being optimized.

With akde() and weights=TRUE and fast=TRUE, you need the dt argument to accurately represent the true sampling schedule's intervals. You have many fixes at around 15 minutes, but with some variability. I would try 15/2 minutes for dt. What does the automated argument come out to be?

Your dataset doesn't appear to be too large, so you can check against the exact calculation with fast=FALSE, to make sure that your dt choice is working. Otherwise, you would want to lower dt into smaller and smaller divisors of the smallest common sampling intervals to check for convergence.

Best,
Chris

messages.subject: Re: Changes in sampling intervals
parts:
Hi Adam,

fast=FALSE,PC='direct' is numerically exact, but its too slow with very large datasets. fast=TRUE with a preconditioner is for improved computational speed on larger datasets. If the distributions look very similar, then you can feel safer rolling out the faster algorithm on your entire dataset, if you need that speedup. But with recent versions of the package, the default fast=NULL will do a pretty good job at choosing good arguments for your dataset.

eobs location accuracy columns should be detected and imported into the telemetry HDOP column, with the point estimate of the location error set to 1 meter. You want to put a prior on that, as detailed in the vignette('error'): https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/ctmm/vignettes/error.html
Then you would want to turn error on in the guess, but not modify that after fitting.

For the coati dataset, this would look like the following:

data(coati)
UERE <- uere(coati) # copy over error structure
UERE$UERE # here there is only one location class 'gps' - your data may differ
UERE$UERE[,'horizontal'] <- 1.4
UERE$DOF[,'horizontal'] <- 2.5
summary(UERE,level=0.5)[,,'horizontal'] # most e-obs are between 1 and 1.6
uere(coati) <- UERE # calibration data would be preferred

GUESS <- ctmm.guess(coati[[2]],CTMM=ctmm(error=TRUE),interactive=FALSE)
FIT <- ctmm.select(coati[[2]],GUESS,trace=3)

summary(FIT)

Best,
Chris

All of the default algorithms in ctmm are O(n) or O(n log(n)), meaning that computation time scales linearly or almost linearly with the amount of data. Analyzing the individual with 42k locations should only take 10 times longer than analyzing an individual with 4k locations. So, assuming everything is working right, being patient should work.

fast=FALSE,PC='direct' is numerically exact, but its too slow with very large datasets. fast=TRUE with a preconditioner is for improved computational speed on larger datasets. If the distributions look very similar, then you can feel safer rolling out the faster algorithm on your entire dataset, if you need that speedup. eobs location accuracy columns should be detected and imported into the telemetry HDOP column, with the point estimate of the location error set to 1 meter. You want to put a prior on that, as detailed in the vignette('error'): https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/ctmm/vignettes/error.html

data(coati)
UERE <- uere(coati) # copy over error structure
UERE$UERE # here there is only one location class 'gps' - your data may differ
UERE$UERE[,'horizontal'] <- 1.4
UERE$DOF[,'horizontal'] <- 2.5
summary(UERE,level=0.5)[,,'horizontal'] # most e-obs are between 1 and 1.6
uere(coati) <- UERE # calibration data would be preferred

GUESS <- ctmm.guess(coati[[2]],CTMM=ctmm(error=TRUE),interactive=FALSE)
FIT <- ctmm.select(coati[[2]],GUESS,trace=3)

summary(FIT)

Chris
